minutes.headline: Select Board interviewed two interim Town Manager candidates and chose Mr. terenzini first, Blanchard second, unanimously.
minutes.summary: The board interviewed two candidates for interim Town Manager, Charlie Blanchard and Carter terenzini, asking the same questions about availability, budgets, town meeting, hiring and management style. In discussion, members agreed both were qualified, and all leaned to terenzini partly because he has no stated hour limit. They split up reference checks, asked the Town Council-side staff to draft an agreement and get salary ranges, and voted a first and second choice before adjourning.

votes.motion: Name Mr terenzini as the board's first choice and Mr Blanchard as second choice for interim Town Manager.

budget_items.what_was_said: Members noted the line item and reserve left in the budget limit what can be offered, and the candidates know this. Salary requirements and ranges for both candidates are to be requested.
A candidate said the town has remaining ARPA money that must be committed by the year-end deadline, and suggested using the capital list or state bid list.
A candidate described closing a gap in another town after the cherry sheet arrived.
A candidate described a failed override in another town where the finance committee and board were not aligned.
A candidate described an override for capital improvements that was never appropriated in the same year.

budget_items.topic: Interim manager hours and pay structure
budget_items.what_was_said: Blanchard proposed a salaried arrangement based on a committed number of weekly hours at a fair hourly rate, with actual hours often higher. Members discussed roughly 25 to 30 hours a week.

decisions.decision: Reference checks for the lead candidate will be split among board members, with each calling a different reference, and results shared only as 'checks out' unless a problem is found.
Julie is to draft an interim Town Manager agreement based on the last interim agreement and request salary requirements/ranges from the candidates.
The board will take up the vote on the agreement at a short, possibly front-loaded meeting, with availability to be coordinated by text, allowing remote attendance by a member on vacation.
Blanchard will be asked for a reference list as a backup.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted unanimously to name Mr. terenzini its first choice for interim Town Manager and Mr. Blanchard its second.
The board interviewed two interim candidates, Charlie Blanchard and Carter terenzini, asking each the same questions on availability, budgets, town meeting, hiring and management style.
Members will split the reference checks for the lead candidate, each calling a different reference, and report back only if a problem turns up.
Julie is to draft an interim agreement based on the last one and request salary ranges from both candidates.
The board will vote on the agreement at a short meeting, possibly front-loaded, with dates to be arranged by text and remote attendance allowed.

why_it_matters: The interim Town Manager will run town operations and prepare budget work while the permanent search continues, so this choice shapes who handles the next budget cycle.
Members said the budget line and reserve for the position limit what can be offered, so the pay in the agreement draws on a fixed amount of town money.
